blocking.fix: Pick one payload semantics and state it once. I recommend: delete `result` as a named location from oracle/lproc declarations; introduce a distinct internal step-state register `result_val`, initially 0, whose width is the signature `tgt` width; define `lift.retval v` as `result_val ^= v` (v any readable location/pseudo-location) and commit from `result_val`. For `lift.ret`, deliver by exchange, not XOR: copy the operand value into a dedicated frame disp slot before exchanging L_f back, then swap that slot with the unique location whose id equals record.dest (the slot retains dest's old value); state the inverse in that order and count the slot in k_max. Also state the declaration order that defines L_f and location ids (params, then regs, in text order, per function in index-space order). The alternative — payload is the named result location, `lift.retval` writes nothing and its operand MUST be that location, and call destinations MUST be provably clean — also works but forces producers to zero destinations before every call in loops, so take the exchange version.
blocking.problem: `lift.retval` is defined as `result ^= v`, commit XORs `result` into tgt, and both examples declare `result r` naming the location that already holds the answer and emit `lift.retval r`. If `result` is that location, the row computes r ^= r = 0 and inc8 returns 0, contradicting its own text; if `result` is a distinct internal register, the `result r` declaration and §3.7's `result: reg[T]` are meaningless and §14.1 never says the payload is v. Two executors will pick differently. The same defect recurs in `lift.ret`: it XORs `record.v` into the destination although the record layout in §3.7 has no v field, no rule says which record cell holds the operand after the L_f exchange, and XOR is not assignment — for a destination location holding a nonzero old value (any second call in a loop) the step construction yields old XOR v where the reference interpreter, which alone defines F_B, assigns v. Construction and reference therefore compute different functions.

blocking.fix: Remove both invented readings rather than normativising them, since C semantics is pointer-based (the same reason the editor declined region-named loads). Rewrite @sum: take the database base as an explicit third parameter threaded through the recursive calls (or materialise it with lift.const in each activation), and read the global the ordinary way — a pointer constant for its layout base, lift.boundscheck, lift.load.i8 — or compare against a lift.const 0 location if no global read is needed. State the closed name-resolution rule in §3.7: a read operand in a lifted row is exactly a location of the containing function or an interface pseudo-location (in/args) of the containing oracle; lproc bodies see only their own locations plus the oracle's in/args pseudo-locations, never its mutable locations; a global's name is not an operand. Recompute the example hashes under the rewritten body.
blocking.problem: Example 2 is not well-formed under §§3.7/4.2 and its commentary invents two semantic rules found nowhere else: `zero` used as a read operand 'denotes a lifted load of its image width at its base' with a boundscheck the dialect 'emits' (but the object holds only the reference body, so those rows, and their budget steps, either exist or do not), and @sum reads `base`, a mutable location of the enclosing oracle, justified only by the sentence 'lprocs read the enclosing oracle's locations as pseudo-locations'. 'Enclosing oracle' is undefined for an lproc linked into several oracles or called from another lproc, nothing says whether the read sees the value at oracle entry or the current value, and §3.7 defines pseudo-locations as interface inputs only, never writable — oracle locations are writable. A producer and an executor will disagree on whether this body is legal, what it reads, and how many steps it takes.
blocking.section: §3.7 pseudo-locations, §4.2 read operands, §16.3 Example 2 and its commentary

blocking.fix: Give lift.load/lift.store the same flag as lift.boundscheck for their own address and length: flag = (p >= 2^H) or not-exists live entry containing [p, p+N/8), computed without wrap at max(ptr_width, Hc) bits; C = FAULT_UB_MEMFAULT; successor HALT on flag; the access (assignment) executes only under not-flag. Keep lift.boundscheck as an explicit assertion row for compatibility — after a dialect-emitted boundscheck the load's own flag is never set, so reference step counts and F_B for dialect-produced bodies are unchanged — and state in §14.1 that the reference interpreter applies the identical check. The alternative, a suite-F rule requiring a dominating boundscheck with identical (p, n) operands before every access, also restores totality but makes legality depend on a dataflow check two verifiers must implement identically; take the inherent check.
blocking.problem: Nothing requires a lift.boundscheck before lift.load/lift.store in a well-formed body (§5.1 lists no such rule; it is only a property of bodies the dialect mapping produces). For a syntactically well-formed oracle that loads at an input-derived address >= 2^H or outside every allocation, the reference interpreter (§14.1, cells 'are arrays') has no defined value, while the §7.2 construction uses 'the low H bits' and wraps into a live cell — two different functions, and T1's claim that F_B is defined for every well-formed oracle is false. A hand-written or competitor-produced object, which the spec exists to admit, hits this immediately.

blocking.fix: Add the missing side conditions to §5.6 and to the §12 toggling_lemma witness check: X is disjoint from the borrowed set and from W's targets; every gate of V has its target in the borrowed set and all its controls in X (V touches no other wire); the sets of W's targets and W's controls are disjoint as sets (not merely per gate). With those four clauses the affine argument goes through and the counterexample is excluded because b2 is borrowed, hence not in X. Add the counterexample to suite F as a negative test for the witness checker.
blocking.problem: The toggling lemma as stated is unsound. It never requires X to be disjoint from the borrowed set, never states that V's controls lie in X and its targets only in the borrowed set, and condition (ii)'s 'outside W's own controls' does not say whether target/control disjointness is per-gate or over all of W. Counterexample satisfying all four printed conditions with borrowed {b1, b2}: V = cx b2 b1 (XORs into a borrowed wire a function of X = {b2}); W = cx b1 t (writes no wire of X, target outside X/borrowed/controls, one borrowed control); frame V;W;V^-1;W leaves t ^= (b1 XOR b2) XOR b1 = b2. The public output depends on a borrowed value and entangles with it, yet a structural certificate claim of kind toggling_lemma would label this proof — exactly the failure mode opus round-3 B3 raised, now in the replacement rule.

blocking.fix: Define log2inv_eps as the exact integer min{k >= 0 : eps * 2^k >= 1} for 0 < eps <= 1 (load error outside), state each op's arity, and state that a table index outside the array is a load-time error. Replace free-form scheme wires with an indexed wire grammar: a scheme declares control wires c[0..k-1], one target t, optional parameter theta, and aux wires a[0..m-1] with m given by an expression in k; template gate entries are {gate, wires: indexed forms such as c[i], a[i+1], t, params: expressions over theta/k/i}; repeat is from-inclusive to-exclusive over integer i. Make `schemes` an ordered array (with a name field) so 'first' is defined, and state that a schedule's scheme reference resolves to that array entry. The restricted alternative — schemes only for fixed arity with fully explicit wires, one entry per k — is also implementable but cannot express MCX families, so take the indexed grammar.
blocking.problem: Target expressions still cannot be evaluated identically by two parties. `log2inv_eps` has no definition: as a real log2(1/eps) it is generally irrational, contradicting exact-rational evaluation (suite E), and the grammar gives it an args list without arity. Scheme templates cannot be expanded: template wires are plain strings like 'c0' with no rule binding them to an actual gate's k controls, no indexed-wire syntax for a repeat body to reference c[i] or an aux wire, no statement of whether repeat's to bound is inclusive, no way to pass a gate parameter (an RZ decomposition needs theta/2), and no declaration of how many aux wires a scheme needs or of what class. 'First schemes entry' is also undefined because schemes is a JSON object. A vendor and a scheduler cannot produce the same gate sequence or the same cost from this format, which was codex B8 / muse B7 in substance.

blocking.fix: State the convention the examples in fact use (so the printed hashes stand): part (5) is two consecutive groups — first every reached data entry sorted by data name, written `NAME SP HEX LF`; then every reached layout sub-entry sorted by dotted name, written `<dotted name> SP <JCS encoding of its value> LF` (a scalar's JCS encoding is its decimal text). Move the layout sub-entry line format from the §16.3 commentary into §9.2. State that part (6) lists only references leaving the symbol's SCC, in first-reference order, each as 64-hex LF; intra-SCC references contribute no part-(6) line and are replaced by @$i in parts (4)-(5) wherever an @name token occurs. Define the reached layout set mechanically: the scalar fields H, A_tab, S_cells, null_size, heap_base; every globals entry (all of them initialise alloctab, matching @sum_db); and, for an oracle, its own interface_regions entries. I verified inc8 byte-for-byte under the printed rule and reproduced @sum/@sum_db only under the convention above, which is why it must be printed.
blocking.problem: The semantic envelope is not byte-reproducible from §9.2's text. Part (5) says data entries and layout sub-entries are included 'sorted by name', without saying whether the two classes are merge-sorted by name or emitted as two sorted groups; a layout sub-entry has no 'JCS line' (the layout section is one object) — its `<dotted name> SP <JCS or INT>` line format appears only in Example 2's commentary; part (6) requires the hash of every referenced symbol, which is circular for an SCC member, and the SCC paragraph says intra-SCC 'references' are replaced by @$i without stating whether that replacement happens in part (6), or part (6) omits intra-SCC references, or includes a placeholder line; and which layout entries a symbol 'reaches' is judgement-based (@sum_db's envelope includes globals.zero, which its own body never addresses, but excludes the zero data line). Plausible readings give different hashes for the same object, so certificates and deduplication still do not interoperate in the general case.

blocking.fix: Make small-width numerical claims checker-computed rather than witness-trusted: state that for metric operator_norm the checker builds the realised and reference unitaries itself at the stated widths in interval arithmetic (basis order = allocation order, §14.2), forms interval enclosures of V-dagger U - I entrywise in row-major order, and derives the bound by the Frobenius-norm upper bound computed in interval arithmetic at precision_bits — the witness is then only {widths, precision_bits, bound} and is a checkable assertion about the recomputation, not data to trust. For metric diamond, either add an SDP dual-certificate schema (dual variable as an interval Hermitian matrix in stated order, with the PSD/feasibility checks the checker performs) or state that diamond numerical claims are evidence in this draft and only exhaustive/channel claims computed by the checker are proof; I recommend the evidence downgrade now and the dual schema as a named extension. Key `error` by '<variant>:<inherited_controls>' exactly as `cleanup` is keyed, and give the rule-specific witness fields for inverse_pair_library (the library entry's closure hash) and adjoint_table (no fields).
blocking.problem: The certificate still does not let an independent checker verify its numerical and some structural claims. A numerical claim's witness is `{"intervals": [...]}` with no statement of what the intervals enclose (matrix entries of what operator, in what basis order), how an operator-norm or diamond bound is derived from them, or how a checker 'recomputes' them without an algorithm — for diamond norm, an SDP optimum, no dual/feasibility witness format exists at all, so any array of numbers is an acceptable-looking 'proof'. Structural witness fields are given only for toggling_lemma; inverse_pair_library names no way to identify the library certificate it rests on. And `error` is a single {metric, value} per region although realised error depends on variant and inherited control count (the very keying §6.4 mandates for schedules and that cleanup entries have), so composition in §12.3 combines numbers that may belong to different variants.

blocking.fix: Define specificity as a total order and conflicts as errors: an entry beats another if it is greater in the lexicographic tuple (path length, iteration non-*, phase non-*, generated non-*, kind-field present), and two incomparable maximal entries that both match one generated op make the schedule invalid (not first-wins, so encoder order is never semantic). Define iteration for every generated class: for a static point inside qloop, its 0-based dynamic repetition count within the invocation; for oracle-generated ops, the forward step index t in 1..B, with phase rev denoting the inversion of step t (executed in decreasing t); add an optional `generated_index` selecting the ordinal of the generated op within its source row's normative expansion, default '*', and require a gate entry whose realisation names a scheme to select only gates that scheme realises. State that an entry may instead be interpreted uniformly only when generated_index is '*'.
blocking.problem: The hierarchical schedule cannot yet be executed verbatim by two consumers. 'More specific entries override less specific ones' is a partial order: an entry specific in path and another specific in iteration can both match one generated operation with no stated winner, and document order is not declared significant or insignificant. `iteration` is undefined for the largest generated class — the B steps of an oracle and their prefix-reversal counterparts (does iteration count forward step t, reversed order, or loop repetitions of the source point?) — and `generated: gate` selects all gates a row expands to, although a single row expands to gates of different opcodes (dispatch comparators, arithmetic, exchanges) for which one scheme realisation cannot apply to all. A validator cannot tell whether such a schedule is legal, and two executors will realise, and charge, different circuits from it.
blocking.section: §11 schedule document and obligations, suite H

blocking.fix: Choose one of two stated semantics. (a) Segment uncall, which I recommend if in-program reversal is wanted: form `uncall @f (args) (results)`; it finds the most recent unreversed call segment for @f whose recorded boundary args and produced results equal the current values of the named operands (all classical, so checkable), deletes that segment from the history reversing its memory/alloc/effect/Q-call frames exactly as in §10's tree, and leaves caller frames recorded after the segment (e.g. a copy of the result) in place; if no segment matches it is a CC trap / R fault record FAULT_UB_TRAP; executing uncall itself pushes a frame recording the segment id so whole-run reversal re-executes the call. (b) No in-program uncall: delete the instruction and state that call reversal exists only as the §10 run/tree operation and as LIFO trace reversal, renaming §9.4's convention accordingly. Either is defensible; (a) preserves the Janus-style compute-copy-uncall idiom the reversible tier will want, (b) is smaller. What cannot stand is an unlabelled pop with a silent precondition.
blocking.problem: The in-program `uncall` instruction (§4.1) has no operands and its only semantics is §7.4's 'reverses the most recent unreversed call whose frames are the top of the history'. After a call returns, any intervening instruction — including the copy of a result that is the usual reason to uncall — pushes a frame, so the call's frames are no longer the top; the spec does not say whether uncall then traps, faults, searches down the history for a segment, or is statically ill-formed, nor how the call's result instances (the call is both a 'defining instruction' frame and a 'call boundary' frame, with no stated order) are treated. Two executors will implement different machines, and a producer cannot know where uncall may legally appear.

criteria.change: Fix result/return delivery (B1) and close the read-operand name-resolution rule (B2); those are the two places where the drawn state diagram still has two readings.
criteria.evidence: Tiers, state table, index-space flattening, frame layout, separate size exponents and wider counters (Hc/Ac/Sc/Dc), and the monotonic stack now let two implementers draw nearly the same machine (§§3.2-3.7). It breaks at the edges of that machine: whether `result` is a location or an internal register (§3.7 vs §§4.2/16.3), and which names a lifted row may read — Example 2 reads a global's name and the enclosing oracle's mutable location under rules stated only in its commentary.

criteria.change: Give load/store rows their own bounds flag (B3) and define `uncall` as a named segment operation or delete it as an instruction (B9).
criteria.evidence: The §4.2 row table with class/flag/successor columns, the §3.3 operand schema and width rules, and full-interface lifted call forms are a large step toward a closed set. Gaps remain where an implementer must guess: lifted load/store have no semantics outside a live allocation absent a preceding boundscheck, `uncall` has no operands and no stated failure mode, and lift.div's code choice ('DIV0 or SDIV_OVERFLOW') is left to inference.

criteria.change: Add the disjointness side conditions to the toggling lemma (B4); a one-clause fix to a now-unsound structural proof rule.
criteria.evidence: The assignment/direct row classification, all-computed-before-exchange parmov, fault writes in the inverse, halted self-loop, only-retval success, commit/prefix-reversal, memory-aware transfer rules, and matched oracle_uncall make the coherent semantics mostly checkable (§§3.6, 5.2, 5.5, 6). But the step construction disagrees with the reference on return delivery (B1), and the new structural borrow rule certifies a frame whose output depends on a borrowed value (B4), so one stated proof rule is false as printed.

criteria.change: Give scheme templates an indexed wire grammar with parameter expressions and define log2inv_eps as an exact integer operation (B5).
criteria.evidence: The JSON AST with exact-rational numbers, variables k/eps/a/w/c, first-match gate entries with inclusive control ranges, per-kind aggregation, a timing model, and an imports map are the right shape for a vendor format (§8). It still cannot be consumed identically: log2inv_eps is undefined and generally irrational under exact evaluation, and scheme templates have no indexed-wire binding, parameter passing, or aux declaration, so the main parametric family (MCX) cannot be written down.

criteria.change: Print the envelope's group ordering and SCC part-(6) rule in §9.2 (B6); hashes are the load-bearing identity every other contract binds to.
criteria.evidence: Section schemas, a complete-looking C surface with builders/accessors and ownership, the invocation-tree reversal model, and a hierarchical schedule are all present now (§§9-13); I reproduced inc8's interface hash byte-for-byte and @sum/@sum_db under one convention. But that convention (data-group before layout-group, intra-SCC references omitted from part (6), the layout sub-entry line format) is not what §9.2 literally says, numerical certificate witnesses remain uncheckable shapes, and schedule override precedence is a partial order.

criteria.change: Restore T1 by making lifted accesses inherently checked (B3), so the reference interpreter is total on exactly the well-formed bodies.
criteria.evidence: T1-T6 are stated with hypotheses, the reference interpreter is normative and sole definer of F_B, domains D/exhaustive-sampled-structural-numerical claims and suites A-H map cleanly onto the text (§§12, 14, 15). T1 is nonetheless false as quantified — a well-formed body can load outside every allocation with no reference value — and a numerical 'proof' can be an arbitrary intervals array, so conformance cannot yet distinguish proof from assertion there.

criteria.change: Rewrite Example 2 to use pointer-based global access and explicit lproc parameters (B2), so the worked example embodies the address-dispatch decision instead of contradicting it.
criteria.evidence: No contradiction with the north star's settled points remains: two region interfaces, reference-defined F_B and budget unit, exact-permutation oracle tier, validity as Silq/Unqomp discipline, QCM-style synchronisation via the halted self-loop, content identity over a semantic envelope. The residual friction is self-inflicted: the example's global-by-name read reintroduces by-name memory access the editor explicitly declined for lifted loads, and stack-limit exhaustion reports FAULT_BUDGET_DEPTH, muddying the north star's distinct-code-per-cause rule.

criteria.change: Move every rule currently living in §16.3 commentary (layout sub-entry lines, reached-set membership) into the sections that own it, and add the toggling counterexample and an unchecked-load body as negative suite-F cases.
criteria.evidence: A VM or specialiser author could start tomorrow on the core: state, rows, construction, transfer rules, headers and one verified hash example are all in place, and the deferred list (§17) is genuinely non-semantic. They would stop at the points where normative content hides in example commentary (hash sub-entry format, pseudo-location readings) or is still a shape rather than a rule (scheme templates, interval witnesses, schedule precedence).

path_to_accept: Nine bounded edits, no redesign: (1) introduce a distinct internal result_val, delete `result` as a location, and make lift.ret deliver by displaced exchange with the L_f/id order stated (B1); (2) close lifted read-operand resolution to own locations plus oracle in/args pseudo-locations and rewrite Example 2 with an explicit base parameter and pointer-based global access, recomputing hashes (B2); (3) give lift.load/lift.store the boundscheck flag as an inherent check so the reference is total (B3); (4) add the toggling lemma's disjointness clauses: X disjoint from borrowed and W-targets, V controls in X and targets only borrowed, W targets and controls disjoint as sets (B4); (5) define log2inv_eps as an exact integer, give schemes an ordered array with indexed wires, parameter expressions and aux counts (B5); (6) print the envelope convention the examples use — data group then layout group, layout line format, intra-SCC omitted from part (6), mechanical reached set (B6); (7) make numerical claims checker-recomputed at small widths with a stated norm derivation, key error by variant:controls, and complete structural witness fields (B7); (8) give schedule matching a total specificity order with conflicts as errors and define iteration/generated_index for generated ops (B8); (9) define uncall as a named segment operation with a mismatch fault, or remove the instruction (B9). With those stated I would return accept.
suggestions: State explicitly that oracle entry initialises atop to the number of pre-entered (global + mapped-region) alloctab entries and heap_used/sp/fp/depth to 0; §5.2 step (1) implies it for alloctab contents but never says the counter is set, and boundscheck reads i < atop (§§3.7, 5.2, 7.2).

Give stack-limit exhaustion its own fault code (FAULT_BUDGET_STACK = 11, F >= 5) instead of reporting the monotonic-stack condition in lift.call as FAULT_BUDGET_DEPTH, matching the north star's distinct code per budget cause (§§4.2, 5.4).
Pin lift.div's code selection in one clause: DIV0 iff b = 0 (any of the four opcodes), SDIV_OVERFLOW iff signed and a = MIN and b = -1 (§4.2).

Add the missing opaque typedefs bennett_sched_request_t and bennett_sched_response_t to the §10-§11 header, and state bennett_wait's discrimination convention (exactly one of result_out/request_out is non-null) plus a way to observe SUSPENDED, since suspend takes effect asynchronously at a CC boundary (§§10, 11).

Give qborrow a §6.1 transfer row: the borrowed bundle is `other` (or explicitly exempt from provenance, governed solely by §5.6 frames), so no cleanup obligation or window is ever inferred for it (§6.1).

Reject the all-zero xoshiro256** seed in sampled claims (it is a fixed point) and state the sampler mapping arithmetically: value = lo + m where m is the first consumed output's low ceil(log2(hi-lo+1)) bits that is < hi-lo+1 (§12.1).

Fix the exhaustive claim's table encoding: each output is an array of decimal strings giving the full final tuple in signature order — ins, tgt, fault, mut bundles, then each region's cells by index, then borrowed — so two checkers compare the same tuple T3 names (§12.1).

Say what happens for an unknown or wrong-region budget token and for oracle_call operands whose widths/roles mismatch the callee signature when this is only detectable at run/launch time: a named load error (suite F) or BENNETT_E_BUDGET/E_ARG at bennett_run (§§4.7, 10).

Use the full ISA version (isa=0.4, not MAJOR isa=0) as envelope part (1) while the ISA is pre-1.0, since minor drafts change semantics and would otherwise share interface hashes across incompatible rules; this changes the example hashes, so do it in the same pass as B2/B6 (§9.2).
summary: Round-3 resolution accounting. Resolved as raised and not re-raised: codex B3 (null region, pinned pre-entries, distinct bases, heap bound, address-range dispatch, same partition in CC/R), B4 (region threading, operand schema, width rules, full call interfaces), B5 (predicate/control-context and interface-memory transfer rules, qstore/qexchm provenance, sequence-bound cleanups), B6 (oracle_uncall consuming successor versions under a shared invocation identity), B11 (invocation tree with exactly-once reversal, hostcall, eligibility, close); muse B3, B4, B5 (device ops over (ptr,len), entropy tape as run input), B6; opus B1 (base-only match for lift.free, counter widths separated from size exponents, max(n,1)), B2 (layout partition with shim heap base and mapped interface regions), B5 (flattening by closure hash, lift.label as sole index source, qbranch a terminator, lift.ret at depth 0 faults). Resolved in substance with only suggestions left: codex B12 and the header part of muse B8 (builders/accessors/ownership present; two sched typedefs and wait discrimination still unstated). Re-raised in part, because the fix is incomplete or introduces a new defect: codex B1 and muse B1 — row classes and fault-write inverses are fixed, but return delivery still disagrees with the reference (B1_RETVAL_RET_DELIVERY here); codex B2 and muse B2 — index space, counters, records and dest ids are fixed, but record.v and result are undefined and Example 2 invents global-by-name and enclosing-oracle reads (B1, B2_NAME_RESOLUTION); codex B7 — dynamic SSA instances and device/fault encoding fixed, but the `uncall` instruction's own contract is unstated (B9_UNCALL); codex B8 and muse B7 — AST/rationals/tables fixed, but log2inv_eps and scheme expansion remain undefined (B5_TARGET_SCHEMES_AND_LOG); codex B9/B10, muse B9, opus B4 — envelopes, schemas and example hashes are a real advance (I verified inc8 byte-for-byte, and @sum/@sum_db under the data-group-then-layout-group, intra-SCC-omitted convention), but §9.2's text does not state that convention, so identity is not reproducible in general (B6_ENVELOPE_ORDERING_AND_SCC); codex B13 and the schedule part of muse B8 — hierarchical selectors exist, but precedence is a partial order and iteration is undefined for step-machine ops (B8_SCHEDULE_SELECTOR_SEMANTICS); codex B14 and muse B10 — domains, sampler and typed errors fixed, but numerical witnesses are still an uninterpreted intervals array, structural witness fields are incomplete, and error is not keyed by variant (B7_CERTIFICATE_WITNESSES); opus B3 — the V;W;V^-1 rule was correctly withdrawn, but its toggling-lemma replacement omits the disjointness conditions and certifies the counterexample in B4_TOGGLING_LEMMA_DISJOINTNESS. One further new blocker: lifted accesses without a preceding boundscheck are undefined in the reference yet wrap in the construction, falsifying T1 (B3_UNCHECKED_LIFTED_ACCESS). The draft is a full grade better than 0.3 in structure, but two executors would still build different machines at returns, borrow certification, targets, identity and scheduling, so the verdict is revise.
